correctness.rationale: The transfer matrix yields exact stationary PSD with the stated Fourier normalization. Its scalar derivative has the monotone-sign numerator -z^2-2cz+a^2b^2-c(a^2+b^2), so c<a^2b^2/(a^2+b^2) is necessary and sufficient for exactly one positive-frequency maximum; equality has none. AM-GM gives the exact optimized rho threshold and attaining gain. Independent Fourier inversion gives a slower negative and faster positive exponential in every peaked unequal-decay case, hence one positive covariance zero; the repeated-eigenvalue formula gives a single linear bracket and the same conclusion. The explicit rho=-4/5 example is exact. Replayed 3,058 numerical checks support the identities but are not relied on for their infinite parameter ranges.

value.rationale: A PSD peak is commonly used to infer oscillatory feedback or a complex deterministic mode. The theorem supplies an exact necessary-and-sufficient parameter boundary for a robust countermechanism with only real decay modes; the strongest allowable correlation boundary after optimal coupling is explicit and independent of forcing intensities. The resulting single covariance sign reversal distinguishes a spectral band-pass artefact from repeated damped cycles. This is a natural all-parameter class and a useful caution for interpreting finite-frequency noise, rather than a one-off numerical example.
